coverage.diagram_kind: normalized point-blowup resolution chain with empty-chain and regular-curve cases
coverage.finding: The multi-stage construction is a reasonable optional diagram candidate: it distinguishes the initial normalization from later normalized point blowups, records the finiteness condition needed for properness, and ends at a regular scheme. The definition is already readable in the preview, so this is an editorial recommendation, not a defect.

main_chain: Initial arrow nu:S^nu=S_0 -> S, labelled normalization and finite (required by the definition).
For i=0,...,n-1, choose a closed point s_i in S_i with nonzero coherent point ideal; show S_{i+1}=Bl_{s_i}(S_i)^nu -> Bl_{s_i}(S_i) -> S_i.
Mark each intervening normalization as finite; then each composite stage S_{i+1}->S_i is a proper birational modification.
Label the composite S_n->S proper and birational and mark S_n regular. Do not claim the construction exists for every integral S; the source defines its shape only.
special_cases: If S is normal, nu:S^nu->S is an isomorphism and the chain starts effectively at S.
If S is regular, show n=0 and S_0=S^nu=S; the resulting resolution is the identity, with no point-blowup stages.
separate_dimension_remark: Keep the regular-surface and regular-curve remarks in a separate inset from the resolution chain.
For a regular point on a regular surface, the blowup is generally non-isomorphic and has exceptional fibre P^1; it remains regular and its normalization is the identity.
For a closed point on a regular one-dimensional integral scheme, its ideal is invertible and its blowup is an isomorphism. The source says this need not hold on a singular curve.
checks: The arrows point from each new normalized blowup S_{i+1} to its preceding stage S_i, with the initial normalization arrow S^nu->S at the right end of the displayed chain if following X=S_n->...->S_0->S left-to-right.

Properness of each normalized point-blowup stage relies on finiteness of its normalization morphism; the source explicitly declines to assert properness where finiteness has not been established (lines 90-93).
Do not conflate the surface blowup with the regular-curve blowup: their exceptional fibres and isomorphism behavior differ.
diagram_details.scope_caveat: This is a schematic of the definition and its stated examples/caveats, not a proof of existence of a resolution or a universal assertion about arbitrary blowups and normalizations.
